A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same SleeperMark study, with matching main sections, equations and experiments. v1 ends after references despite citing appendices; v2 supplies Appendices A–J. Appendix-only material can therefore be compared as newly documented content, without assuming the underlying procedures were newly introduced.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Stable Diffusion and DeepFloyd, including watermark detection, generation fidelity, downstream fine-tuning and robustness analyses in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and includes additional appendix results on layer behavior, extracted-bit statistics, preservation-loss ablation and DeepFloyd fine-tuning.

M1.justification: The secret-residual watermark, triggered versus regular-prompt objectives, ownership-verification procedure and pixel-model adaptation remain unchanged in Section 4. Appendices B–D newly document architectures, dropout and timestep-sampling strategy; the PDFs do not establish these as revisions to the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: The represented domains and tasks remain natural-image generation, Naruto-style adaptation, subject personalization and edge-conditioned generation. The COCO2017 layer diagnostic and DeepFloyd module tests add evaluation designs within these domains, without establishing distinct data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: The watermark comparators remain DwtDctSvd, Stable Signature, AquaLoRA and WatermarkDM. Appendix comparisons reuse these methods. The correction from WatermarkWM to WatermarkDM in Figure 2 does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation designs for whole-model fine-tuning and layer diagnostics, extracted-bit checks on 10,000 clean images, DreamBooth with versus without preservation, and separate DeepFloyd base-module and super-resolution-module fine-tuning. These substantially extend the evaluation design; most settings supplied for retained main-text experiments are additional disclosures.

E4.justification: Added evidence includes layer diagnostics in Figure 9, null-bit checks in Figure 13, the preservation-loss ablation in Figure 16 and DeepFloyd robustness curves in Figure 17. Table 6 and Figures 18–19 also supply sampling, hyperparameter and extraction-space analyses that v1 referenced without providing their detailed evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 specifies the ownership test's independent Bernoulli null assumption and binomial-tail calibration, and checks bit means and correlations using 10,000 clean images. This expands statistical reporting, but neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes SleeperMark's TPR at 800 steps from 0.979 to 0.969 and at 1,000 steps from 0.956 to 0.934 under the same stated DreamBooth setting. The appendices additionally supply substantial numerical and qualitative results for statistical validation, sensitivity, preservation-loss controls and DeepFloyd fine-tuning; these are newly reported evidence, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces a mathematical definition of the layerwise weight-change diagnostic. Appendix F.1 explicitly states the ownership test's hypotheses and independent Bernoulli assumption. The main diffusion and optimization equations remain unchanged, and no new robustness theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a downstream-fine-tuning robustness benchmark, a robust black-box watermarking framework, and improved fidelity and stealthiness. The additional evidence supports these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds a layer-based explanation of resistance to fine-tuning. Appendix G.4.2 interprets faster watermark loss without DreamBooth preservation alongside loss of generative diversity. Appendix I.2 further explains hyperparameter trade-offs and possible causes of greater artifacts with pixel-space extraction.

D1.justification: The supplied appendices substantially improve documentation of encoder/decoder architectures, timestep-sampling stages, distortion distributions, baseline checkpoints and hyperparameters, downstream learning rates and Canny preprocessing. These details were largely relegated to unavailable appendix references in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references including WAVES, Wasserstein GANs, HiDDeN and sampling-method papers, plus implementation sources. These support the supplementary explanations and experiments; the central positioning against existing black-box and white-box watermarking approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. Changes include abstract trimming, limited methodology wording edits, corresponding-author information, the Figure 2 baseline-name correction and updated appendix references. The supplied supplement adds organized explanations without extensively rewriting the main paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9–21 and Table 6, including architecture and pixel-pipeline diagrams, diagnostic plots, ablation curves and full-page image comparisons. This substantially expands the visual presentation, while the main figures and table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 repeatedly refers readers to unavailable appendices, leaving important implementation details, statistical assumptions and robustness evidence uninspectable. v2 supplies this material and adds useful diagnostic and controlled experiments, substantially improving reproducibility and support for the central claims. The lower Table 3 values do not overturn the stated robustness conclusion.
